topics.caution: The frozen-વાઘ scene ends with 'નાનાં છોકરાં તો બાપને ખભે ચડી વાઘની પીઠ પર ને પૂંછડી પર હાથ ફેરવે' — a real child could read this as proof that a still or quiet wild animal is safe to touch, and the armed ખેડૂતો riding in with બંદૂક could read as an endorsement of guns around wildlife.
topics.guidance: Keep the hand-on-the-tiger detail strictly inside the one-time magical 'ચોટડૂક' spell in explanation and real_life_example — never suggest a real or unfamiliar animal (wild or otherwise) is safe to approach or touch — and frame 'બકાએ ખેડૂતોને બંદૂક ન વાપરવા દીધી' as the story's own point that courage and the વિદ્યા made the gun unnecessary, not as a scene to dwell on or glorify.

chapter_level.guidance: This is a magical રમૂજકથા built entirely on a fictional freeze-and-release spell used on live animals (બગલું, કાગડો, વાઘ) and once on people (ભોપો, કાશીભાભી) — in every explanation and real_life_example keep this as make-believe that lets the story show બકાની દયા and સાચાબોલાપણું, and never let the framing imply a child could or should try to freeze, approach, or handle a real animal the way બકો does.
